study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Segal et al., Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging, 2025
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Multiscale Heterogeneity of White Matter Morphometry in Psychiatric Disorders

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study applied warped Bayesian linear regression (WBLR) normative models using the PCNtoolkit (version 0.21). B-spline basis expansion over age was used to model non-linear effects, and likelihood warping was used to model non-Gaussian and heteroscedastic imaging phenotypes.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We applied warped Bayesian linear regression normative models to T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging data; we used normative modeling to obtain person-specific WMV deviation maps relative to a model, based on Bayesian linear regression with likelihood warping (31), of population expectations for voxelwise WMV variations (see https://github.com/amarquand/PCNtoolkit, version = 0.21); B-spline basis expansion over age was used to model non-linear effects, and likelihood warping was used to model non-Gaussian and heteroscedastic imaging phenotypes.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Segal2025.pdf.md: ABSTRACT; Methods and Materials / Voxel-Scale WMV Heterogeneity; 1-s2.0-S2451902225001272-mmc1.pdf.md: Supplementary Methods / Normative modelling

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled voxelwise white matter volume (WMV) estimated using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) of T1-weighted anatomical MRI scans. The normalized segmented white matter images were modulated and spatially smoothed with an 8mm FWHM Gaussian smoothing kernel.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: We estimated voxelwise WMV using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) of T1-weighted anatomical MRI scans; voxel-wise WMV was estimated using the Computational Anatomy Toolbox (CAT12 r113); The normalised segmented white matter images were modulated and spatially smoothed with an 8mm full width at half maximum (FWHM) Gaussian smoothing kernel.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Segal2025.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Voxel-Scale WMV Heterogeneity; 1-s2.0-S2451902225001272-mmc1.pdf.md: Supplementary Methods / Anatomical data

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model predicted WMV as a function of age, sex, and scan site. B-spline basis expansion over age was used to model non-linear age effects. Site was included as a covariate to handle site effects.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we fitted separate models to each white matter voxel to predict WMV as a function of age, sex, and site; B-spline basis expansion over age was used to model non-linear effects; To handle the site effect, we included scan site as a covariate
